newsitem.title: USA: CSCE world sugar ends slightly up in dull trade.
newsitem.headline: CSCE world sugar ends slightly up in dull trade.

text.p: CSCE world sugar futures settled firmer with activity focused on the nearby switch, trading sources said.
"It's all May/July activity," a dealer said, noting trade buying in the spread.
Today's close just under the day's highs may signal further gains are in story on Wednesday, traders said.
Volume was estimated at 26,541 lots, compared with Monday's official 22,533 lots.
The last trading day for the May contract is April 30.
Resistance in most-active July remained at Friday's high of 11.18 cents, above which level Brazil is expected to emerge as a seller.

The most-active July contract ended up 0.04 cent per lb to 11.12 cents per lb, having ranged from 11.13 to 11.04 cents. May rose 0.03 on the day to 11.27 cents, while the outer months closed unchanged to 0.02 higher.

In fundamental news, Belarus said today it will buy 180,000 tonnes of raw sugar in 1997 compared with 150,000 tonnes in 1996. The country's annual domestic refined sugar needs total about 300,000 tonnes.
((-- S Rostler, New York Commodities Desk, 212 859 1640))
